# morar <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/viniciusoike/morar/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/viniciusoike/morar/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

morar computes housing affordability under Brazilian mortgage rules. It
answers two questions: how much income a household needs to buy a given
property, and how expensive a property a given income can buy. It handles
SAC, Price and mixed amortization, effective and nominal rates, insurance
(MIP and DFI) and administrative fees. Every core function is vectorized, so
it works on whole income or price distributions inside `dplyr::mutate()`.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("viniciusoike/morar")
```

## Income and price

`min_income()` returns the monthly income needed to finance a property, and
`max_price()` inverts it. By default the first payment may take 30% of
income, and the loan-to-value ratio follows Caixa's SBPE limits for the
chosen method.

```{r}
library(morar)

# Income needed for a R$ 500k property at 11% a.a., SAC, 80% LTV
min_income(500000, i = 0.11)

# Most expensive property each income can finance
max_price(c(5000, 10000, 20000), i = 0.11)
```

Banks approve credit against the first payment *including* insurance and
fees. MIP depends on the borrower's age, so the charges default to zero;
pass your own rates to include them.

```{r}
min_income(
  500000,
  i = 0.11,
  mip_rate = 0.0003,
  dfi_rate = 0.00008,
  admin_fee = 25
)
```

`loan_summary()` returns every component at once:

```{r}
loan_summary(c(300000, 500000, 800000), i = 0.11, method = "price")
```

## Amortization schedules

`amortization_table()` builds the month-by-month schedule for one loan.

```{r}
amortization_table(500000, i = 0.11, n = 420, admin_fee = 25)
```

## Affordability indices

The Housing Affordability Index (HAI) compares a household's income with the
qualifying income: 100 means it qualifies exactly. The price-to-income ratio
(PIR) divides the price by annual income and maps to the Demographia
categories.

```{r}
calc_hai(price = 400000, income = 8000, i = c(0.08, 0.11, 0.14))

pir <- calc_pir(price = 500000, income = 10000, annual_factor = 40 / 3)
pir
pir_category(pir)
```

## Conventions

- Rates are decimals: `0.11` means 11% a.a. Use the all-in rate; for loans
  indexed to TR, add the expected TR to the contract spread.
- `rate_type = "effective"` (default) compounds the annual rate;
  `"nominal"` divides it by 12.
- Affordability is evaluated at the first payment, the highest one under SAC.
- `ltv = NULL` uses `default_ltv(method)`: 80% for SAC, 70% for Price and
  mixed.
- `calc_pir()` annualizes income with `annual_factor = 12`; use `40 / 3` to
  include the 13th salary and the vacation bonus.
